result:
The proposed answer of 0 is wrong, because its own argument shows M(N) grows like a positive multiple of log N.

The proposed solution's key steps are sound. The walk escapes to infinity, and the time to reach spine level n is of order λ^{-n}, so the deepest level reached by time N is about log N / log(1/λ). The error is in the last step. An upper bound M(N) ≤ i_max(N)+1 = O(log N) does not imply M(N)/log N → 0. The solution never shows that cut times are sparse among the levels visited.

They are not sparse. A cut time at spine edge i→i+1 occurs when the walk, after first reaching (i+1,0), never returns to (i,0). Side excursions always return, so the effective spine walk has up-probability 1/(1+λ) and down-probability λ/(1+λ). From (i+1,0) the probability of ever hitting (i,0) is λ, so the probability of never returning is 1−λ > 0 at each level. Future vertices at levels above i are disjoint from the past, so this is exactly the cut condition. Hence a positive fraction of the spine levels visited by time N give cut times, and M(N) ~ c·log N with c > 0 (heuristically c = (1−λ)/log(1/λ), though I have not verified the constant rigorously). The almost sure limit is therefore positive, not 0.

VERDICT: REJECT
CONFIDENCE: 4
